mappings.note: Defines isomers and draws both butane isomers - 'structural formulae ... and their isomers' is LO-4 of C 1.3 exactly.
Soap in hard water, detergent composition and the advantage of detergents - all three parts are the soap-versus-detergent distinction of LO-9.

POOR FIT. Preparation of ethanol by hydration of ethene. LO-8 covers ethanol's properties, not its preparation, and the reactant here is ethene, which no outcome mentions; LO-8 cited as the nearest legal code.
Advantages of synthetic detergents over soap - the distinguishing clause of LO-9.
Scum formation from Ca and Mg ions. Mapped to LO-9 because failure in hard water is what separates soaps from detergents; the saponification code LO-8 has nothing to say about it.

Three parts: the bromine-water test for unsaturation and the substitution explanation both fall to C 1.3 (no outcome covers addition or substitution), while the products of burning ethanol are LO-8. C 1.3 leads on two parts out of three.
Parts (a) and (c) are naming and homologous-series membership (C 1.1-LO-4); part (b) is the alcohol/sodium reaction (C 1.2-LO-8). Two of three parts sit with LO-4, so it leads.
Equations (a) and (b) are ethanoic acid and ethanol chemistry (LO-8); equation (c) is the methane/chlorine substitution, which no outcome covers, hence C 1.3.

Asks for one example each of substitution, addition and oxidation. The subject is the reaction CLASSES themselves, none of which has an outcome, so C 1.3 alone - even though the oxidation example happens to be ethanol.
Identifies ethanol from the sodium test and then gives its dehydration - two properties of the named compound, LO-8.
Ethanoic acid with bicarbonate, oxidation of ethanol, and hydrolysis of the ester (saponification). All three are LO-8 content, so one code carries the item.
Defines 'functional group' and identifies two of them - the first clause of LO-4.
Preparation of vinegar by oxidising ethanol in air is LO-8 content; the 'what is fermentation' half has no code in this frame, which is why the code is not a complete fit for the item.
POOR FIT. Commercial preparation of ethanoic acid from methanol and CO. Industrial preparation is outside every outcome (and outside NCERT); LO-8 cited only because it names ethanoic acid.
Ethanoic acid with sodium carbonate and with sodium hydroxide - chemical properties of the named acid, LO-8.
Oxidation of ethanol by chromic anhydride to ethanal. Still an oxidation of ethanol, so LO-8, though the product is ethanal rather than the ethanoic acid the outcome names.
Ethanol with alkaline KMnO4 giving ethanoic acid - the ethanol-to-ethanoic-acid oxidation named in LO-8.
Three uses of acetic acid. LO-8 is the only code naming ethanoic acid; uses sit at the edge of its 'properties' wording.
Identification puzzle resolved by ethanoic acid's sodium reaction and its esterification with ethanol - both LO-8 reactions.
Decarboxylation of sodium ethanoate with soda lime to give methane. Preparation of an alkane has no outcome; mapped with the other soda-lime item (sha 0b74b1d80703a81c) under C 1.3.
Sodium test for an alcohol - the ethanol/sodium reaction used diagnostically, so LO-8 rather than C 1.3.
Laboratory demonstration of saponification (ester layer disappearing with NaOH). Saponification is named in LO-8; LO-9 would apply only if the soap's cleansing behaviour were examined.
Why linear-chain detergents are environmentally preferable - a detergent property, and LO-9 is the only code covering detergents.
POOR FIT. Two-step fermentation of molasses with equations. This is the preparation of ethanol, which no outcome covers; the largest item of the fermentation cluster flagged in the report.
Ethanol as antifreeze, oxidised to ethanoic acid (C2H4O2). Both the identification and the reaction are LO-8 content.
